title: Retrospective: curb tenant-driven queue amplification and restore autoscale responsiveness
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary: On 2026-02-28 we observed sustained queue buildup and latency amplification across multiple hosted GPU pools after a partial model rollout and a simultaneous tenant workload spike. Symptoms: elevated request queue length, token-level throttling, increased 429s for lower-priority routes, and slow autoscaler response. Impact: 18 minutes of degraded tail latency for 12% of production requests; several high-throughput tenants experienced request failures and client-side timeouts.

Root cause analysis (high level):
1) Tenant workload change: a large customer launched a new heavy-batched inference job that invalidated prefix/KV cache heuristics and produced surgey decode lengths.
2) Autoscaler regression: a recent autoscaler change (scale cooldown logic) increased the scale-up convergence time under rapid, bursty alloc patterns. The cooldown prevented timely pod allocation for affected GPU pools.
3) Admission policy gap: tenant admission scoring did not account for expected decode length and KV cache miss rate, so the scheduler prioritized throughput over fair tail-latency protection, causing amplification of queue length when cache locality dropped.
4) Insufficient synthetic coverage: no existing synthetic test reproduced simultaneous KV cache invalidation + scale-up churn, so the regression wasn't caught in CI.

What worked: fallback to smaller quantized model variants reduced OOM risk for some tenants; emergency manual prewarm by SRE shortened impact window.

Action items (concrete, owners, acceptance criteria):
- AI1: Implement token-aware admission scoring (owner: Aisha Patel) — incorporate expected decode tokens + cache-miss penalty into admission score so long-decoding requests are deprioritized when queue length grows. Acceptance: simulated burst test shows 30% reduction in 99.9th latency for mixed workloads. Target due 2026-03-12.
- AI2: Revert/patch autoscaler cooldown regression (owner: Marco Ruiz) — change: make cooldown backoff proportional and add fast-path scale-up when queue_growth_rate > threshold. Acceptance: scale-up median time reduces to <= 45s under synthetic surge. Target due 2026-03-10 (hotfix done), follow-up QA in runtime-1.21.
- AI3: Add KV-cache-invalidating synthetic harness (owner: Priya Nair) — CI job that simulates prefix churn and validation of cache-miss amplification. Acceptance: CI catches a labeled regression within 1 day of introduction. Target due 2026-03-20.
- AI4: Route-level soft caps and graceful failover (owner: Omar Haddad) — per-tenant soft queue caps with automatic reroute to cheaper model variant and early-fail options. Acceptance: no more than 1% increase in client errors during surge and 50% fewer 429s on low-priority routes. Target due 2026-04-01.
- AI5: Telemetry & alerting improvements (owner: Aisha Patel) — new Grafana panels: queue_growth_rate, admission_drop_rate, kv_cache_miss_ratio, autoscaler_convergence_time; alert thresholds tuned. Acceptance: SRE-runbook triggers accurately within 2min of incident start in test. Target due 2026-03-15.
- AI6: Incident runbook and chaos test (owner: SRE rotation) — documented step-by-step containment + automated chaos test to exercise scale-up under KV churn. Acceptance: runbook reviewed and signed off by SRE/Runtime PM. Due 2026-03-18.

Planned rollout/ship plan: hotfix autoscaler cooldown (runtime-1.20.3) already deployed 2026-03-05. Token-aware admission scoring will land behind feature flag and be enabled progressively on a single low-traffic pool for 72h, with metric burn-in. Full rollout contingent on CI harness and grafana alerts.

comments: 2026-03-02 — Liam Chen: Initial incident summary and triage notes added. Assigned to Aisha for admission scoring and Marco for autoscaler regression. Added high-level action list and linked hotfix PR.

2026-03-03 — Marco Ruiz: Autoscaler cooldown hotfix deployed to canary pools; observed scale-up improvement in canary (p95 scale-up 72s -> 40s). Will push hotfix to prod on 2026-03-05. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7482
2026-03-05 — SRE rotation: Hotfix rolled to prod at 03:12 UTC. Incident tail latency improved; residual 429s limited to under-2% for low-priority routes. Marked immediate mitigation complete.

2026-03-07 — Priya Nair: Drafted synthetic harness for KV churn (tests/prefix_churn_sim). Local runs reproduce queue amplification with current autoscaler config. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tests/pull/312

2026-03-08 — Design review (Mariela Soto): Reviewed admission scoring UI for Console (per-route indicators). Suggested adding explicit "expected decode tokens" column in route table. Created follow-up DES ticket: DES-211.

2026-03-09 — Aisha Patel: Implemented initial token-aware admission scoring behind feature flag. Canary enabled on pool-gamma. Early signals: admission_drop_rate reduced for short requests; long decodes queued but no 99.9 spike. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/6521

2026-03-10 — Customer Success (Nina Park): Informed affected customers of incident and mitigation timeline; provided temporary best-practices (batch size limits, model-variant fallback). No customers requested compensation at this time.
2026-03-11 — Liam Chen: Postmortem draft posted to Confluence. Asking reviewers: runtime, autoscale, SRE, PM. Deadline for feedback: 2026-03-14.

2026-03-12 — Marco Ruiz: Autoscaler follow-up: implemented queue_growth fast-path and integrated with prewarm controller. Unit tests added; perf benches show median scale-up 38s under synthetic surge. Needs canary validation before full rollout. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/284
